title: How many turns fit a three-arm figure with equal gaps?
description: A three-arm figure with one hundred twenty degrees between neighbouring arms is turned, with one arm coloured to follow it. The red arm is moved onto each place in turn and the turns are added up to the full turn. Keeko's doubt is that only one hundred twenty degrees counts.
teaching_notes: One idea: keep adding the gap between neighbouring arms until the full turn is reached, and every sum is an angle of symmetry. Watch for students who list only the gap itself.

source: A 3-arm figure has 120° between adjacent arms. How many angl
video_script.why: The child lists all the angles of symmetry of a three-arm figure with equal gaps by adding the gap again and again.
video_script.substitution: the book's three-arm figure with colours added to follow the arms through each rotation
video_script.anchor: the book's three-arm figure with one hundred twenty degrees between neighbouring arms
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred twenty is the only angle of symmetry
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts only the gap between neighbouring arms and stops there.
video_script.payoff_line: The figure has three angles of symmetry

final_answer.spoken: three angles of symmetry: one hundred twenty, two hundred forty and three hundred sixty degrees

maths_rules: 3 equal arms with 120° between neighbouring arms, 3 x 120 = 360
turn by 120°: each arm lands on the next arm, so 120° is an angle of symmetry
120 + 120 + 120 = 360: the figure is back at the start
the angles of symmetry are 120°, 240°, 360°, which is 3 angles
video_script.design: The three-arm figure with a red, a blue and a green arm. The arms are followed through each turn, and the sums of the gap are written one under the other. Keeko's doubt is that only the gap counts.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the three-arm figure with 120° marked between neighbouring arms, one arm red, one blue, one green

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.fig: the three-arm figure appears with 120° marked between neighbouring arms
marks.ask: the question glows under the figure

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, about a three-arm figure.
<bookmark mark='fig'/>The angle between neighbouring arms is one hundred twenty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many angles of rotation does it have, and what are they?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the three-arm figure with its dot; a curved arrow round the dot; the words angle of symmetry

marks.fixed: the dot at the centre lights up
marks.name: the curved arrow and the words angle of symmetry appear

narration: <bookmark mark='fixed'/>The figure turns about the dot at its centre.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A turn after which it looks exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry.
The colours help us follow each arm.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 equal radial arms; angle between neighbouring arms = 120°
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the figure has three equal radial arms.
The angle between neighbouring arms is one hundred twenty degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many angles of rotation, and what they are
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many angles of rotation it has.
We also name each one.

beats.on_screen: turn by 120°: the red arm lands where the blue arm was, and the figure looks the same

marks.one: the figure turns by 120° and the red arm lands where the blue arm was
marks.same: a tick appears: the figure looks the same

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, turn the figure by one hundred twenty degrees.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Each arm lands where the next arm was.
The figure looks the same, so this is an angle of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: 120° + 120° = 240°: turn by the gap once more; the figure fits again

marks.two: the figure turns by the gap once more

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, turn by the same gap once more.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>One hundred twenty plus one hundred twenty is two hundred forty degrees.
The figure fits again.

beats.on_screen: 120° + 120° + 120° = 360°: the full turn, every arm is back at the start

marks.three: the figure turns by the gap a third time
marks.sum: 120° + 120° + 120° = 360° is written and every arm is back at the start

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, turn by the gap a third time.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>One hundred twenty plus one hundred twenty plus one hundred twenty is three hundred sixty degrees.
Every arm is back at the start.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The figure has three angles of symmetry.
They are one hundred twenty, two hundred forty and three hundred sixty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the figure
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble from Keeko says 120° only; the figure turns by the gap twice and the red arm lands on the third arm; the bubble is struck out

marks.again: the figure turns by the gap twice and the red arm lands on the third arm

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one hundred twenty is the only angle of symmetry, because that is the gap.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Turn the figure by that gap twice, and the red arm lands on the third arm.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The figure looks unchanged there too, so more turns count, and the doubt is cleared.
